opening.summary: The Sicilian's ...c5 challenged d4 without copying ...e5; subsequent exchanges determine how each side uses the resulting space and files.

sections.title: White's plan
sections.text: White's e-pawn takes central space while Black's c-pawn challenges d4. In an Open Sicilian, playing d4 exchanges a central pawn for Black's c-pawn and opens lines for active pieces. Delaying d4 keeps different structures available. The useful question is how White can finish development while making that central space count.

sections.title: Black's reply
sections.text: Black creates an asymmetric center rather than copying White's e-pawn move. If the c-pawn is exchanged on d4, the c-file can become a route for the rooks, provided other pieces don't block it. Black's counterplay has to accompany development and king safety; the opening's reputation doesn't make an unprepared attack sound.
